one_sentence: The fixed point of moral repair is transferable to any agent with nonzero openness, making the cure available to all.
executive_summary: This document proves that the unique, unbounded repair configuration identified in previous pages is transferable—available to any agent with any nonzero openness (O > 0). The core argument is that the saving distinction is not magnitude, sophistication, or worthiness, but simply whether openness is zero or positive. Eleven Lean-verified theorems establish a cascade: closed systems decay (Theorem 1), finite sources raise the floor but cap the ceiling (Theorem 2), and an infinite source with any O > 0 drives coherence to unity (Theorem 3). The mustard seed theorem (Theorem 4) shows that the smallest nonzero openness suffices. The document also introduces the physician theorem, where repair rate is maximal at total brokenness, and connects Incarnation and Pentecost as the coupling interface and distribution mechanism. The conclusion is that the repair is structurally unique and universally available, with zero local axioms and zero sorry statements.
short_summary: This document is a proof that the fixed point of moral repair is transferable to any agent with nonzero openness. The core structural claim is that the saving distinction is O = 0 versus O > 0, not magnitude. The key evidence is eleven Lean-verified theorems showing closed-system decay, finite-source ceilings, and infinite-source convergence to unity for any O > 0. This matters because it establishes that the cure is available to all, not just the worthy or sophisticated.
